A: **Demo Line vs Fix-and-Check** 1. Failure Wall: post last week's failures; electrician narrates fixes while visitors watch. 2. Skill-Value Circle: pick weekly queue for most new skill per minute; fixers repair, strangers check. Circle wins: builds transferable skill, not spectatorship. Example: 12 chairs in trios; visitor Maya fixes toaster cord, then checks stranger's kettle plug against checklist while electrician only confirms. Test: two Saturdays alternate formats; following week invite back without appliances and ask each to diagnose unseen faulty lamp. Circle must yield more correct independent fixes.
B: **Joint Peak vs Lease Turns** 1. Synced Peaks: both play lively on shared clock blocks, pause together. 2. Crowd Lease: alternate holder on wall-clock; holder plays lively, other plays sparse for 15 minutes, then yield. Lease wins: prevents mutual starvation under volume cap. Example: 7-10pm, even quarters Ana holds north with chorus, Ben south fingerpicks; odd quarters swap; watches checked at :00/:15/:30/:45. Test: compare one lease night vs one both-full night using case coins per 15 minutes at each end. Lease must show higher minimum take and smaller end-to-end gap.
C: **FIFO Stack vs Fair Ledger** 1. Nightly Shuffle: play random tapes three hours, discard rest. 2. Fair Ledger: number each tape at drop-off, log every play publicly, fill nights least-played first, re-queue errors next night. Ledger wins: guarantees eventual airing, correctability, traceability. Example: Tuesday airs least-played #14-#22 for three hours; morning posts list on door; #19 cut short returns top of Wednesday queue; owner sees number. Test: run each for one week; compare oldest unplayed wait and top-voice share. Ledger must lower both versus Shuffle.
D: **Keep Wall vs Link Cards** 1. Salvage Yard: store large beams in new bridge, each stamped with donor crossing story. 2. Link Cards: give each daily crosser one rivet-chip card to annotate with date crossed and memory, then pin linked cards by route, season, ritual. Link Cards win: cheaper, daily-shaped, survivable. Example: commuter Ana links her 6am chip to her father's fishing chip; both cast into new parapet concrete with QR lineage. Test: for one season offer both; count distinct daily crossers contributing and links created per dollar. Link Cards must beat Yard by 3x.
